transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I'm here because... I've been having this issue with eating. What really brings me in is how I feel after I do it. I'll just sit there looking at all the empty wrappers and containers, and I feel completely disgusted with myself. I've always tried to be a steady, in-control kind of man, and... well, doing this makes me feel like I'm not that guy at all.
After you eat, do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives or diuretics to prevent gaining weight?
No, I don't do anything like that. I've never made myself throw up, and I don't take any of those pills or laxatives. I just... I just sit with it, and deal with feeling miserable afterwards.
Do you often feel sad, hopeless, or lose interest in things you used to enjoy, especially around the time you're eating this way?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I feel pretty terrible about myself right after it happens, like I mentioned, but... I don't feel hopeless in general. I still enjoy my regular stuff. I still like watching the game, getting out on the road for my routes... I haven't really lost interest in my life or anything like that. It's just this one issue.
When you're eating this way, do you feel like you can't control yourself or stop eating even if you want to?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start... it feels like the same discipline I have out on the road just shuts off. Even while I’m sitting there telling myself, 'Magin, put the fork down,' my hand just keeps going back for more. I just can't seem to stop.
When these episodes happen, do you find yourself eating a lot more than most people would in the same situation or in the same amount of time?

Yeah, I definitely do. Some evenings, you know, I’ll heat up what I swear is just going to be one bowl of pozole. But before I know it, I’ve gone through the whole pot. Then I'm eating a couple of tamales, chips, and just whatever leftovers are sitting there in the fridge. It's... it's honestly like I’m feeding a whole crew instead of just myself.
How often do these episodes happen, and do they always happen in private or do they sometimes happen even when you're around other people?

It almost always happens when I'm by myself. I make sure I'm alone when I eat like that. As for how often... well, since I’ve been stuck at home with my back injury, it’s been happening several nights most weeks. I honestly can’t think of a single week in these past three months where I didn’t have at least one of those episodes.
Do these episodes or the feelings that come after them affect your ability to function normally, like making you avoid social situations or causing problems at work or home?

Yeah, it's starting to affect things. I was supposed to be mentoring some of the newer drivers while I'm off the road, doing check-in calls with them. But lately, I've just been avoiding their calls. I feel so ashamed about how I'm eating and how far off my routine I've gotten... I just don't want to talk to anyone or have them hear it in my voice. So I just ignore the phone.
Do you feel distressed about these eating episodes even if you're not worried about gaining weight or how your body looks?

Yeah, it definitely bothers me a lot. I mean... I guess I haven't really thought about it in terms of my weight or how I look. I'm a bigger guy anyway, from sitting in a truck all day. But I just feel... really upset with myself after it happens. 

It's more about the fact that I'm doing it at all and just can't seem to stop myself, rather than worrying about what the scale says. So yeah, it's definitely distressing to me, even without the weight part.
